title: How do three parallel lines give x and y?
description: Three lines are parallel, and a transversal crosses them. An angle of fifty five degrees and x are interior angles on the same side, and y is the corresponding angle of x. A closing check adds x and the given angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: interior angles on the same side add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, and a corresponding angle on the next parallel line is equal. Watch for the perpendicular line, which is not needed.

video_script.why: The child uses interior angles on the same side and then a corresponding angle, as in the solved example, on a figure with three parallel lines.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: AB parallel to CD, CD parallel to EF, EA perpendicular to AB, angle BEF is fifty five degrees
video_script.anchor: three parallel lines AB, CD and EF, the line EA perpendicular to AB, the transversal BE, angle BEF marked 55°, and the angles x at B and y where BE crosses CD
video_script.payoff_line: One pair of interior angles gave both x and y

final_answer.spoken: x is one hundred and twenty five degrees, and y is one hundred and twenty five degrees

maths_rules: AB is parallel to EF and BE is a transversal, so x and angle BEF are interior angles on the same side and add up to 180
y is the corresponding angle of x where BE crosses the parallel line CD, so y = 125
the perpendicular EA is not needed for x and y
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video. The pair of interior angles is filled in one colour, and the corresponding angle y takes the colour of x.
